parsed.explanation: No trans-specific criminal provision, no documented incident or enforcement action, and a functioning court system that has actually granted equality relief (immigration recognition of an overseas same-sex marriage on appellate grounds) — recourse shown working for sexual-orientation claims. Broad official participation in Pride, including premier, governor and ministers, is documented social/institutional acceptance, a direct positive. The marriage ban is resident-facing and secondary. Gaps are open questions (facilities, custody, documents, gender recognition) rather than documented exposures; under rule 13 these weigh lightly. Thin trans-specific data and a constitution without enumerated orientation grounds temper, but do not offset, the documented acceptance and working institutions. Extrapolating from no criminalisation + functioning courts + official acceptance lands in reduced risk, modestly below the acceptance-with-protections tier.
